brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from the Changsha area of Hunan, known for keeping green colour in dry leaf, liquor and infused leaf alike.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was named one of Hunan's ten famous teas in 2005. Little more is documented about its history.
processing: Made from improved cultivars given only organic fertiliser, with a temperature-controlled step that brings up the down.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Slender, even, snail-like curled strands of silvery green with visible white down.
taste_profile: Clean and fresh with a returning sweetness.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
